releases.title: Millisecond Waits
releases.description:
A '300ms' wait ran for five minutes. parseWait() in the scribe effect tested endsWith('s') before endsWith('ms') — and because 'ms' also ends with 's', the millisecond branch was unreachable. Every millisecond-suffixed wait was multiplied by 1000, so a scribe sequence with a {wait: '300ms'} step appeared to stop after the first render.

Seconds ('2s') and raw numbers were unaffected, which is why it went unnoticed — the workaround was to pass milliseconds as a number. This was reported in the v0.25.2 notes as queued for a future patch and has been present ever since.

Internal: the helper was closure-local inside scribe() and therefore impossible to test. It is now a module-scope export, matching resolvePalette, pinned by tests that fail if the branch ordering is restored. The public Domma.effects surface is unchanged.

releases.title: Working Scaffolds & a Real Reactivity Showcase
releases.description:
Fixed — every scaffolded project rendered unstyled. The kickstart templates were written in Bootstrap class names while Domma ships Tailwind-style utilities, so 143 class usages across 14 files resolved to nothing. Anyone who ran npx domma init got a project that looked broken on first load. Two components were dead rather than merely unstyled: the contact FAQ and docs pages used Bootstrap's collapse markup, and Bootstrap JS is never loaded — while contact.js and docs.js already called Domma.elements.accordion() and .tabs() against markup they could not recognise. Both work now.

The Reactivity showcase is a showcase, not a reference. It had six sections, every one named after a mechanism and opening by explaining it — no statement of the problem, no benefit, no guidance on when not to use it. Now twelve sections named for outcomes, demonstration before explanation, opening with the code you stop writing, and a When not to reach for it section that shows the traps running live. Prose grew from 506 to 4,118 words; all 26 interactive demos preserved. See the Reactivity showcase.

New: Try-it panes — editable code with live output on any showcase page — plus the .list-none and .no-underline utilities.

Internal: the template compiler moved into domma-reactive 0.2.0, completing the extraction milestone that had shipped half-done.

releases.title: Observables, Badges & Readable Buttons
releases.description:
New: M.observable() and M.observableArray() — the reactive primitives beneath Models are now reachable from Domma. Use M.create() when you want a schema, validation and persistence; use an observable when you want one tracked value and nothing else. Both are the same functions published standalone as domma-reactive.

Fixed — components stopped updating. onUpdated() never fired for components whose templates contain no {{ }} bindings, so anything rendering its content imperatively rendered once and then went silent — the model updated and persisted, but the DOM was never told and nothing was thrown. This affected the todo, notes, contacts and markdown examples. Introduced in v0.30.0. Writes made from onUpdated must now converge on a value that compares equal, or the watcher re-triggers indefinitely.

Fixed — unreadable controls. Outline buttons used a transparent background with a color-mix() blend, so their contrast depended on whatever sat behind them and the label could land on its own background. Eighteen showcase rules set a background from a variable no theme overrides, with no text colour at all. .table-responsive was used in fourteen places and defined nowhere. The Reactivity showcase used .form-control and .col-md-*, neither of which exists in Domma.

Known issue: onUpdated still does not fire for fields absent from data() — declare every field you intend to change.

releases.title: Homepage — Domma CMS Point-of-Sale Band
releases.description:
Site Update: A new full-bleed point-of-sale section on the Domma JS homepage, sitting between the feature grid and the Examples section, pitching Domma CMS without leaving the page. The section doubles as a working showcase of the effects library — six different Domma effects fire in choreographed sequence as it scrolls into view.

What's in the band:

  • Looping headline — the Domma.effects.scribe typewriter cycles four pitches: 'Want Domma JS power in a CMS?', 'Meet Domma CMS.', 'Markdown-first. Zero build step.', and 'Self-hosted. Open. Ridiculously fast.' — typing, holding, erasing and retyping in an infinite loop with a blinking cursor.
  • Stat tiles with stagger-in + counter cascade — four key numbers (27 shortcodes, 28 themes, 6 free plugins, 0 build steps) zoom-stagger into view, then Domma.effects.counter ticks each value up. The 'Build steps' tile counts down from 60 → 0 for dramatic effect.
  • Animated CTAs — primary Get Started Free sits clean and bold; secondary See Features uses Domma.effects.pulse for a gentle attention pull.
  • Pastel ticker-tape burst — Domma.effects.tickerTape fires a one-shot confetti burst (40 strips, pastel palette) scoped to the band when it reveals.
  • Float-blob ambient backdrop — both the band and the splash hero now use .bg-ambient-float-blobs for slowly-drifting indigo/blue radial gradients.

Effects choreographed: reveal → scribe (looping) → counter (cascade) → tickerTape (burst) → pulse — all triggered by a single IntersectionObserver with a requestAnimationFrame fallback for elements already in the viewport on initial load.

Accessibility note: Because this section is the pitch, its effects override prefers-reduced-motion via respectMotionPreference: false. The rest of the homepage still respects the user's motion toggle.

Known issue surfaced: The work uncovered an ordering bug in parseWait inside src/effects.js — endsWith('s') is checked before endsWith('ms'), so any millisecond-suffixed wait string is multiplied by 1000 (a '300ms' wait becomes 5 minutes). Worked around in the homepage by passing numeric milliseconds; fix queued for a future patch release.

releases.title: Carousel — Crossfade Mode, Custom Easing & Demo Gradients
releases.description:
Enhancement Release: The Carousel element gains a third transition mode and a fully configurable easing curve, with a small library of decorative demo gradients added to the showcase styling layer.

New transition mode — animation: 'crossfade': Outgoing and incoming slides transition opacity at the same time, briefly overlapping mid-transition. Cinematic and soft, ideal for hero imagery and feature reels where the existing 'fade' (clean swap) reads too abruptly. The outgoing slide remains position: relative for the duration of the overlap so the container holds its height — no mid-transition layout reflow. After the transition completes the incoming slide is promoted to the height-keeper role on a single setTimeout, with destroy-time cleanup.

New option — animationEasing: Any CSS timing function is now accepted ('ease', 'linear', 'ease-in-out', 'cubic-bezier(...)', etc.) and is threaded into both the fade/crossfade opacity transition and the slide-mode track transform transition. Default remains 'ease' — fully backwards-compatible.

Showcase rebuild: A dedicated Transitions section on the Carousel showcase page now demonstrates fade, crossfade, and a bouncy cubic-bezier easing example with autoplay + hover-pause, so the effects play themselves the moment the section comes into view.

Demo Gradient Palette: Nine reusable decorative gradients added to domma-showcase.css under the .demo-gradient-* namespace, organised by mood — aurora (vivid high-saturation), dusk (cinematic atmospheric), pop (bright energetic). Showcase-internal, not part of the framework's public CSS API.

Documentation: PHPStorm typings (CarouselOptions.animation widened to 'slide' | 'fade' | 'crossfade', animationEasing?: string added); src/CLAUDE.md module reference updated with transition mode descriptions; ELEMENTS.md gains a Transition Modes table and a Demo Gradient Palette reference.

Quick start:

Domma.elements.carousel('#hero', { animation: 'crossfade', animationDuration: 1400, animationEasing: 'ease-in-out' });

releases.title: Chooser — Visual Option-Picker for Forms
releases.description:
Feature Release: A new Chooser form input — Domma's 25th UI component — replacing the visual weight of native radio buttons and checkboxes when a choice deserves richer presentation. Cards or chips, single or multi-select, all four combinations driven by one unified API.

The four-way matrix:

  • Card · single-select — Pricing-plan style; rich tiles with icon, label, description, and corner badge
  • Card · multi-select — Feature picker with checkbox semantics inside the same card layout
  • Chip · single-select — Compact pill row for terse choices
  • Chip · multi-select — Tag picker with full keyboard support

Per-option metadata:

  • icon — any Domma icon name; renders inline
  • description — sub-text under the label (card + comfortable density only)
  • tooltip — hover hint via data-tooltip
  • badge: { text, type } — corner badge in any of five semantic colours, reusing the existing .badge-* classes
  • recommended: true — success-coloured border ring for the highlighted option
  • disabled: true — muted, non-interactive, skipped by keyboard navigation

Visual polish — six top-level options:

  • accent — selected highlight colour; semantic name (primary, success, info, warning, danger) or any CSS colour string
  • accentStyle — five distinct treatments: border (default), solid (filled tile), glow (transparent border + glowing ring), overlay (heavier translucent fill), underline (thick coloured bottom border)
  • glow + glowColour — soft outer glow on the selected option, optional colour override
  • shadow — none / sm / md / lg / xl applied to every option
  • shadowColour — optional shadow tint

Theme awareness: Semantic colours map to existing Domma CSS variables and retint live across all 26 themes × light/dark variants. Custom hex/rgb values become inline CSS custom properties on the chooser root, so they remain consistent across the four matrix combinations.

Form integration: Use type: 'chooser' in any F.create() blueprint and the form pipeline handles validation, model binding, and submission automatically. Required validation treats an empty array as empty for multi-select. Hidden native <input type="radio|checkbox"> elements are emitted when name is set so the value is captured by FormData even with JS disabled.

Accessibility: role="radiogroup" for single-select with arrow-key navigation; role="group" for multi-select with Tab + Space; aria-checked reflects state; disabled options skipped by keyboard; respects prefers-reduced-motion.

CMS Page Editor integration: The page-roller's form-section editor gains a draggable Add Chooser palette tile. Clicking it opens a slideover with a structured editor — field-level inputs, chooser-level toggles, full options editor with add/remove/reorder, six visual-option fields (accent, accent style, glow, glow colour, shadow, shadow colour), and a live preview pane that updates as you type. Save writes back into the formFields JSON textarea (still the canonical store). Click any rendered chooser tile in the canvas to re-open the slideover pre-populated for editing.

Showcase: Comprehensive page at /showcase/elements/chooser/ covering all four matrix combinations, density and columns demos, every per-option flag (with all five badge types), accent colour and accent style galleries, glow and shadow variants, in-form integration, standalone usage, and a long-form tutorial with three real-world patterns (pricing plan, tag picker, theme picker) plus a gotchas section.

Documentation: Full API reference in docs/API.md; blueprint shape and validation in docs/Blueprints.md; feature section with theme-awareness notes in docs/DommaDocumentation.md; PHPStorm typings include ChooserOptions, ChooserOption, ChooserBadge, ChooserInstance, and ChooserSemanticColour.

Quick start:

Domma.elements.chooser('#host', { variant: 'card', options: […] }); — standalone.

F.create({ plan: { type: 'chooser', variant: 'card', options: […] } }).renderTo('#form'); — inside a blueprint-driven form.

releases.title: Ticker Tape — Confetti-Parade Effect
releases.description:
Feature Release: A new canvas-based ticker tape effect joins the Domma.effects family — colourful rectangular strips drop from the top of a container (or the entire viewport), sway, rotate, and gently fade before reaching the bottom. Reminiscent of a ticker-tape parade, perfect for celebration moments.

What it does:

  • Two modes — Pass null for a fixed full-page overlay, or a selector for a container-scoped effect; the canvas reflows automatically via ResizeObserver
  • Theme-aware palettes — The default palette: 'theme' reads --dm-primary, --dm-success, --dm-warning, --dm-danger, and --dm-info from the active Domma theme, so the same call adapts to whichever theme is loaded
  • 10 named palettes — rainbow, festive, gold, silver, pastel, mono, sunset, ocean, forest, and bridal; supply your own array of CSS colour strings for branded confetti
  • Continuous or one-shot — The default mode maintains a steady stream up to density strips on screen; burst: true drops a single batch (burstCount strips) and lets the effect end naturally — ideal for form-success or achievement-unlocked moments
  • Tunable physics — speed, sway, rotationSpeed, strip width / height ranges, and fadeStart (where in the fall fade begins) all adjustable
  • Standard control surface — Returns the same { pause, resume, stop, restart, destroy, isRunning, isPaused } object as every other Domma.effects method; honours prefers-reduced-motion by default
  • Showcase — Dedicated page at /showcase/effects/ticker-tape.html with five demos: theme-aware container, palette picker (live swap), physics customisation sliders, one-shot burst, and full-page overlay
  • Documentation — Full API reference in docs/API.md; PHPStorm typings updated; new party-popper icon added to the seasonal set

Quick start:

Domma.effects.tickerTape(null); — full-page parade in the active theme's colours.

Domma.effects.tickerTape('#stage', { burst: true, palette: 'gold' }); — celebration burst on demand.

releases.title: Signature — Canvas Handwriting Pad
releases.description:
Feature Release: A full-featured Signature element — Domma's 24th UI component — providing a canvas-based handwriting pad for capturing signatures in forms, contracts, and consent flows.

Input & Drawing:

  • Pointer Events API — Unified mouse, touch, and stylus input; pressure-sensitive line width on stylus devices with graceful fallback for mouse and touch
  • Smooth Bézier curves — Midpoint quadratic Bézier algorithm prevents jagged strokes; variable lineWidth per segment from pressure data
  • Normalised co-ordinates — Stroke points stored as 0–1 fractions so a ResizeObserver can reflow all strokes correctly when the container is resized

Undo / Redo & Export:

  • Full stroke history — sig.undo() / sig.redo() operate stroke-by-stroke; sig.clear() is itself undoable; sig.clear(true) for a silent, irreversible wipe
  • PNG export — sig.toBase64('png') returns a canvas data URL
  • SVG export — sig.toBase64('svg') rebuilds paths from stored strokes using the same Bézier algorithm as SVG M, Q, L path commands; output is visually identical to the canvas render

Toolbar & Type Fallback:

  • Configurable toolbar — Colour swatches, pen-width dot buttons, undo, redo, and clear; driven by colours and widths options; hideable with toolbar: false
  • Type fallback — typeFallback: true adds a Draw / Type toggle in the toolbar; Type mode renders cursive-font text to the canvas via fillText() so toBase64() still returns an image; isEmpty() correctly reflects typed content

Form Integration & Config:

  • Hidden input — Auto-populated with the base64 value after each stroke; the component works inside any <form> for native submission
  • Blueprint support — Use type: 'signature' in an F.create() blueprint; the form builder initialises the pad and syncs the model automatically
  • Config Engine — signature added to the component map for declarative $.setup() initialisation

Accessibility: role="application" on the container, aria-pressed on all toolbar buttons, aria-live="polite" status bar, tabindex="0" on the canvas, and respectMotionPreference support.

Showcase: Dedicated page at /showcase/elements/signature/ with 13 sections including a live demo, pen options, export formats, undo/redo, type fallback, disabled state, form integration, config engine, contract-signing tutorial, and full API reference.

releases.title: List Group — Numbered, Horizontal & Selectable Lists
releases.description:
Feature Release: A full-featured List Group element — Domma's 23rd UI component — providing polished, consistent list styling for settings panels, navigation menus, notification feeds, and content lists.

CSS Classes:

  • Base — .list-group container with .list-group-item items; active, disabled, and .list-group-item-action states with hover/focus styling; sub-element helper classes for rich layouts: .list-group-item-icon, .list-group-item-content, .list-group-item-heading, .list-group-item-text, .list-group-item-trailing
  • Variants — .list-group-flush strips outer borders and radius for embedding inside cards; .list-group-sm and .list-group-lg adjust padding and font size; 6 semantic colour variants (-primary, -secondary, -success, -danger, -warning, -info) apply a left-border accent with a tinted background
  • Numbered — .list-group-numbered on an <ol> element prepends auto-incrementing counters via CSS — no JavaScript needed
  • Horizontal — .list-group-horizontal arranges items side-by-side; responsive variants -sm (576 px), -md (768 px), -lg (992 px), -xl (1200 px) switch to horizontal only above the given breakpoint

JavaScript API: E.listGroup(selector, options) enables selectable lists with single or multi-select, roving tabindex keyboard navigation (Arrow keys, Home/End, Enter/Space), and full ARIA semantics (role="listbox", aria-selected, aria-disabled, aria-multiselectable). Public methods: select(i), deselect(i), toggle(i), selectAll(), deselectAll(), getSelected(), isSelected(i), enable(i), disable(i), getItems(), refresh(), destroy(). Callbacks: onChange, onSelect, onDeselect.

Config Engine: listGroup added to the supported component map for declarative $.setup() initialisation.

Showcase: Dedicated page at /showcase/elements/list-group/ with demos covering all CSS variants, numbered lists, horizontal layouts, interactive JS API (selection, multi-select, keyboard navigation), a settings-panel tutorial, API reference tables, and a CSS customisation guide. Linked from the Elements overview page and the Elements dropdown navigation.

releases.title: Number Badge — Notification Counters & Presence Dots
releases.description:
Feature Release: A new Number Badge component extends Domma's badge system with positioned notification counters and presence indicators, available as CSS classes, a JavaScript API, and a <domma-number-badge> web component.

CSS Classes:

  • .badge-number — Standalone circular badge for single digits, expanding to a pill for multi-digit numbers via min-width
  • .badge-dot — Small 8px circular presence indicator (no text)
  • .badge-counter-wrapper / .badge-counter — Wrapper + absolute-positioned counter that overlaps the top-right corner of any element with a border ring
  • 8 colour variants — -primary, -secondary, -success, -danger, -warning, -info, -light, -dark for all three class families
  • .badge-pulse — Reuses the existing pulse keyframe animation for urgent counters

JavaScript API: E.numberBadge(selector, options) wraps the target element in a <domma-number-badge> web component and returns a chainable instance with increment(), decrement(), setCount(), setVariant(), setDot(), setPulse(), and remove(). The badge auto-hides when count reaches zero in non-dot mode, and adds aria-live="polite" and role="status" for screen reader announcements.

Web Component <domma-number-badge>: Shadow DOM custom element with a <slot> for child content. Observed attributes: count, variant, dot, pulse, border-color. Full programmatic API mirrors the JS wrapper.

Config Engine: numberBadge added to the supported component map for declarative $.setup() configuration.

Showcase: Dedicated page at /showcase/elements/number-badge/ with CSS-only variant grids, interactive JS API demo (increment / decrement / dot / pulse / variant controls), web component examples, real-world patterns (mock navbar, inbox unread counts, online user presence list), API reference tables, and CSS customisation guide.

releases.title: Opacity Scale & Translucent Utilities
releases.description:
Enhancement Release: A complete opacity scale and a set of semantic translucency utilities have been added to domma.css, replacing the four sparse .opacity-* classes that previously existed.

Full Opacity Scale: 13 utility classes cover the complete range in steps of 10, with additional quarter-stop values — .opacity-0, .opacity-10, .opacity-20, .opacity-25, .opacity-30, .opacity-40, .opacity-50, .opacity-60, .opacity-70, .opacity-75, .opacity-80, .opacity-90, .opacity-100.

Semantic Translucent Utilities:

  • .translucent-light — Subtle transparency (opacity: 0.85); ideal for watermarks and overlays
  • .translucent — Standard transparency (opacity: 0.70); for modal panels and frosted overlays
  • .translucent-heavy — Strong transparency (opacity: 0.50); for ghost elements

All three classes include transition: opacity var(--dm-transition-normal) so state changes animate without extra CSS.

Frosted Glass: .translucent-glass applies a semi-transparent white background (rgba(255,255,255,0.75)) combined with backdrop-filter: blur(8px) and its -webkit- prefixed counterpart for broad browser coverage. Falls back gracefully to just the transparent background where backdrop-filter is unsupported.

Hover Variants: .translucent-hover, .translucent-light-hover, and .translucent-heavy-hover apply their respective opacity levels only on :hover, with the built-in transition. Useful for image grids and icon buttons.

CSS Custom Properties: All translucency values are driven by five new :root variables — --dm-translucent-light, --dm-translucent, --dm-translucent-heavy, --dm-translucent-glass-blur, and --dm-translucent-glass-opacity — making them straightforward to override per-theme.

Showcase: New dedicated page at /showcase/css-utilities/ with a visual opacity swatch grid, an interactive range-slider demo, translucent card examples, hover-variant demo boxes, a frosted-glass live demo over a coloured gradient, and a full reference table.

releases.title: Card Accent Variant — First-Class `.card-accent` Classes
releases.description:
Enhancement Release: The left-border card accent pattern has been promoted from an inline style workaround to a set of first-class CSS classes, covering the five standard semantic colours.

New CSS Classes:

  • .card-accent — Primary colour left border (4 px), uses --dm-primary
  • .card-accent-success — Success green left border, uses --dm-success
  • .card-accent-danger — Danger red left border, uses --dm-danger
  • .card-accent-warning — Warning amber left border, uses --dm-warning
  • .card-accent-info — Info sky left border, uses --dm-info

Theme Variable Sweep: --dm-card-accent added to all 26 theme files as an alias for the primary colour, enabling per-theme accent customisation and supporting the JS color: 'accent' API option.

Showcase: Dedicated Card Accent section added to the Elements showcase; inline border-left style on the elements index replaced with the new class.

Repo Hygiene: Removed stale backup files (src/css/domma.css.original, public/showcase/css/domma.css.original), stale TODO (public/showcase/elements/CSS_CUSTOMISATION_SECTIONS_TODO.md), empty directories (public/showcase/js/, public/showcase/examples/), and added .superpowers/, firebase-debug.log, and release.json to .gitignore.

releases.title: Christmas — "Frosty Morning" & "Christmas Eve" Theme Overhaul
releases.description:
Enhancement Release: Full palette rewrite of both Christmas theme variants — moving from generic white/slate backgrounds to genuinely festive palettes.

Christmas Theme Overhaul:

  • christmas-light ("Frosty Morning") — Ice-blue tinted backgrounds (#F5F8FC) evoking frost on windows, deep pine-green text (#1A2A1E), classic Christmas Red primary (#C41E3A), rich Holly Green secondary (#2D6B3F), and frosty blue-tinted shadows
  • christmas-dark ("Christmas Eve") — Deep forest green backgrounds (#0A1A10) replacing generic slate, warm candlelight cream text (#F0ECE4), bright red primary (#E85565) for dark-mode readability, bright holly secondary (#5CB875), and warm firelight-tinted shadows

Decorative CSS: Snow-dust radial-gradient dot pattern, red-gold-green gradient card top-borders via border-image, candy-stripe progress bars, and festive syntax highlighting.

Labels: Theme Roller and variant dot tooltips now read "Christmas Day ❄️" / "Christmas Eve 🎄".

releases.title: Wedding — Classic Antique Gold Theme Palette
releases.description:
Feature Release: A new Wedding theme palette — two variants (Day + Evening) built around antique gold (#C5A55A) and silver tones, bringing the total theme count to 26.

Wedding Theme:

  • wedding-light (Day) — Warm cream backgrounds (#FFFDF7), antique gold primary (#C5A55A), antique silver secondary (#A8A9AD), dark warm text (#2C2416), warm tan borders (#E8DCC8), and warm gold-tinted shadows
  • wedding-dark (Evening) — Deep midnight navy (#12121F), gold primary with lighter hover (#D4B66A), warm cream text (#F0E8D8), indigo borders (#2A2A40), and subtle gold-glow shadows

Registered across all surfaces: Available in the Theme Roller dropdown (Day ☀️ / Evening 🌙), the layout variant dot selector (count 24 → 26), the themes showcase card grid, the Kickstart Builder theme picker, and the Domma.theme API (listThemes() / listBases()).

releases.title: Mint — Fresh Spearmint Theme Palette
releases.description:
Feature Release: A new Mint theme palette — two variants (light + dark) built around cool spearmint and seafoam green tones, bringing the total theme count to 24.

Mint Theme:

  • mint-light — Rich eucalyptus primary (#2e9e6e), seafoam secondary (#5b8a7a), white surfaces with a subtle mint-tinted alt background (#f0faf5), near-black forest text (#1a2e25), and soft celadon borders (#c8e6d8)
  • mint-dark — Deep slate-900 backgrounds with a dark mint-tinted surface (#1e3a2f), bright spearmint primary (#6dd5a8) for contrast, mint-tinted text (#d4f5e4), and dark teal borders (#2a4a3a)

Registered across all surfaces: Available in the Theme Roller dropdown, the layout variant dot selector (count 22 → 24), the themes showcase card grid, and the Domma.theme API (listThemes() / listBases()).

releases.title: Auto-Generated Breadcrumbs in the Layout System
releases.description:
Feature Release: The layout system now auto-generates frosted glass breadcrumb pills, overlaid top-left on hero sections and derived entirely from the page URL — no per-page configuration required.

Layout System Breadcrumbs:

  • Frosted glass pill — Semi-transparent black backdrop with backdrop-filter: blur(6px) sits at the top-left of every .hero section; falls back to a surface bar below the navbar on pages without a hero
  • URL-driven label generation — Path segments are mapped through a built-in dictionary (dom → DOM, http → HTTP, spa → SPA, theme-roller → Theme Roller, etc.); anything unrecognised is title-cased automatically
  • Title extraction — The last crumb's label is pulled from <title>, stripping common suffixes such as · Domma Showcase, for a precise page name
  • Preset-driven — Enabled via breadcrumbs.enabled: true in presets.json; active for showcase:subpage, showcase:effects, showcase:element, and public presets; off for landing, index, minimal, admin, and demo pages
  • Responsive — Pill shrinks at ≤576px (font-size 0.7 rem, tighter padding)
  • Two-layer DOM — Outer <nav> holds the pill class; inner <div> is the Domma Breadcrumbs target, preserving component class isolation

Forms Fix: Checkbox fields no longer render a redundant label element alongside the input; the label is now handled by the checkbox markup itself.

releases.title: Forms — Checkbox Label Fix
releases.description: Patch Release: Corrected label rendering logic in forms.js so that checkbox fields are excluded from the standard label output. Previously, a visible label element was injected alongside the checkbox even when the label was already embedded within the checkbox markup, causing doubled text on checkbox-type fields.

releases.title: Grayve — Slate & Steel Theme Palette
releases.description:
Feature Release: A new Grayve theme palette — two variants (light + dark) built around cool slate and steel-grey tones, bringing the total theme count to 22.

Grayve Theme:

  • grayve-light — Steel-blue primary, light slate surfaces, dark navy text, and soft grey borders; a neutral professional palette suited to data-heavy interfaces
  • grayve-dark — Deep charcoal backgrounds, lighter steel primary for contrast, muted slate borders, and off-white text

Registered across all surfaces: Available in the Theme Roller dropdown, the layout variant dot selector (count 20 → 22), the Kickstart Builder theme picker, and the Domma.theme API.

Breadcrumbs CSS Refactor: Inline styles previously injected by elements.js at runtime for .dm-breadcrumbs-item, .dm-breadcrumbs-separator, and .dm-breadcrumbs-link were moved to elements.css as static rules. The separator selector was also corrected from .dm-breadcrumb-separator (singular) to .dm-breadcrumbs-separator (plural) for consistency.

releases.title: Unicorn & Dreamy — Two New Theme Palettes
releases.description:
Feature Release: Two new fully theme-aware colour palettes — Unicorn (pink and purple) and Dreamy (beige and biscuit) — each with light and dark variants, bringing the total theme count to 20.

Unicorn Theme:

  • unicorn-light — Amethyst purple primary (#9b59b6), hot pink secondary (#e91e90), white surfaces with soft lavender tint (#faf5fc), dark aubergine text (#2d1b3d), and light purple borders (#e1bee7)
  • unicorn-dark — Deep purple-black backgrounds (#1a0e24 / #241432), lighter purple primary (#ce93d8) for contrast, lighter pink secondary (#f48fb1), and muted purple borders (#4a2660)

Dreamy Theme:

  • dreamy-light — Warm brown primary (#8d6e63), warm cream surfaces (#fffdf9 / #f5f0eb), dark chocolate text (#3e2723), and light biscuit borders (#d7ccc8)
  • dreamy-dark — Dark espresso backgrounds (#1c1410 / #2a1f1a), lighter taupe primary (#bcaaa4) for contrast, warm off-white text (#efebe9), and dark brown borders (#4e342e)

Registered across all surfaces: Both themes are available in the Theme Roller dropdown, the layout variant dot selector, the Kickstart Builder theme picker, and the Domma.theme API (listThemes() / listBases()). The variant dot count in the layout controls is updated from 16 to 20.

Codebase Cleanup: Removed six stale backup and .bak files (dom.js.backup-*, elements.js.backup-xss-*, three celebration theme .bak files), the one-off debug-wizard.html, firebase-debug.log, the auto-generated coverage/ directory, and the .playwright-mcp/ screenshot cache.

releases.title: Canonical Sweep — SEO, Dead Links & Theme Fixes
releases.description:
Maintenance Release: Resolved Google Search Console's 'duplicate without user-selected canonical' warnings, rebuilt the sitemap from scratch, fixed five dead links across the public site, and corrected theme-awareness in the Blueprint showcase.

Canonical Tags (119 pages): New scripts/add-canonical-tags.js inserts <link rel="canonical"> after </title> in every public HTML page. Root index.html maps to the bare domain URL; subdirectory index.html files use trailing-slash directory URLs; non-index .html files keep their extension. Template fragments (layouts/templates/*, examples/*/template.html) are skipped. The script is idempotent — safe to re-run.

Sitemap Rebuild: New scripts/rebuild-sitemap.js walks public/ and generates a fresh sitemap.xml from files that actually exist on disk. The previous sitemap contained 30+ phantom URLs; the new one has 101 real entries with priority tiers (1.0 root → 0.8 hubs → 0.7 module pages → 0.6 sub-pages → 0.3 legal). Also idempotent.

Dead Link Fixes (5):

  • effects/javascript.html — typewriter.html → scribe.html (effect was renamed in v0.14.x)
  • elements/timer — 'Progress Bar' / ../progress/ → 'Progression' / ../progression/ (component renamed in v0.14.0)
  • miniapps/address — /docs → /api/ (documentation moved)
  • nav-showcase.json — Removed phantom 'Invoicing System' entry (miniapp not yet built)
  • download page — Removed QuickStart Starter card, QuickStart Templates section, and dead quickstart-latest.json fetch() call; all referenced archives are missing

Blueprint Showcase Theme Fix: The example areas (result panes, model state panels, blueprint method badges) were referencing non-existent CSS variables (--dm-bg-secondary, --dm-bg-tertiary) that fell back to hardcoded light-mode hex values, making them appear with light grey backgrounds in every dark theme. Fixed to use the correct Domma variables: --dm-surface-raised, --dm-surface, --dm-primary-bg, and --dm-primary. The code block also gained var(--dm-code-bg) so it adapts in dark themes.

releases.title: DommaComponents — Web Components with Shadow DOM
releases.description:
Major Release: Introducing DommaComponents — a first-class Web Components system built into the Domma framework. Define reusable, self-contained UI components with Shadow DOM encapsulation, reactive state, lifecycle hooks, and scoped styles, all using a clean declarative API.

Domma.component() API:

  • Custom element registration — Domma.component('my-widget', { ... }) registers a native Web Component
  • Shadow DOM encapsulation — Component markup and styles are fully isolated from the host page
  • Reactive data — data() function defines component state; onUpdated() fires on every change
  • Computed properties — Derived values that update automatically when data changes
  • Methods — Event handler functions with access to this.data, this.root, and all Domma APIs
  • Props with validation — Type-checked, default-valued attributes: props: { initialMode: { type: M.types.string, default: 'basic' } }
  • Scoped styles — CSS defined in the style block is injected into the Shadow DOM, invisible to the outside
  • External templates — templateUrl works inside components for substantial markup
  • Lifecycle hooks — onBeforeMount, onMount, onUpdated, onUnmount

Four Example DommaComponents:

  • <domma-calculator> — Scientific calculator with basic/scientific modes, memory functions, angle toggle, and full keyboard support
  • <domma-todo> — Full CRUD task manager with priorities, status tracking, search, and localStorage persistence
  • <domma-markdown-editor> — Real-time markdown editor with live preview pane, syntax helpers, auto-save, and keyboard shortcuts
  • <domma-notes> — Rich note manager with categories, full-text search, overlay editor, and persistent storage

Each component is a single component.js file with a companion template.html, downloadable from the Examples pages and droppable into any project with a single tag.

Components Showcase: New dedicated showcase at /showcase/components/ with live demos, API reference, pattern documentation, and a full tutorial covering all component features.

Splash Page — Examples Row: Eight example tiles now appear on the landing page above MiniApps, each showing a description via Scribe typewriter animation on hover.

releases.title: Theme Renaissance - Complete Theming Overhaul
releases.description:
Major Release: Complete rebuild of the theming system achieving perfect theme-readiness across all 16 themes with full persistence support.

Theme Engine Persistence:

  • Auto-save/load — Theme selections now persist across sessions and automatically load on page refresh
  • Fixed initialization — Removed explicit theme parameters that were overriding stored preferences
  • Seamless continuity — Users' theme choices respected throughout the application

Semantic Variable Migration:

  • Replaced ~298 palette variables (--dm-gray-*, --dm-slate-*) with semantic theme variables
  • Components now use --dm-text, --dm-surface, --dm-border, --dm-hover-bg
  • Semantic variables automatically adapt to each theme's color scheme

Unified Dark Mode Detection:

  • Introduced data-mode attribute set by theme engine
  • Replaced 78+ inconsistent selectors with unified [data-mode="dark"]
  • Consistent dark mode styling across entire component library

Theme File Corrections:

  • Fixed ocean-light/ocean-dark and forest-light/forest-dark file content swaps
  • Improved contrast in 5 dark themes (charcoal, silver, lemon, christmas, sunset)
  • Converted opaque status colors to RGBA tints for better dark theme integration

Component Enhancements:

  • Navbar & Footer: Dark hover backgrounds (#1e293b) with white text in light mode
  • Rounded corners: Changed hover border-radius from sm to md for more polished appearance
  • Visual borders: Added 1px borders to navbar/footer for clear separation
  • Card headers: Improved dark mode contrast with darker backgrounds

Bug Fixes:

  • Fixed splash hero, login tabs, navbar branding, and cookie consent theming
  • Corrected misuse of --dm-text-inverse variable
  • All 298+ palette variable references replaced with theme-adaptive semantic variables

Impact: Zero text visibility issues. All components work perfectly across all 16 themes with proper contrast and readability.

releases.title: Template Evolution - External Template Loading
releases.description:
Major enhancement to the SPA Router: Views can now load HTML templates from external files using templateUrl and partials, dramatically improving code organisation and maintainability.

Key Features:

  • External Templates — Reference .html files instead of embedding large HTML strings in JavaScript
  • Template Caching — Templates fetched once and cached per session for optimal performance
  • Parallel Partials — Reusable template sections loaded concurrently
  • Mustache Syntax — Full support for {{variable}}, {{#if}}, {{#each}}, and {{> partial}}
  • Organised Structure — Recommended js/views/templates/ directory pattern

Impact: Views with 400+ lines of inline HTML reduced to ~50 lines of clean JavaScript. HTML files get proper syntax highlighting and editor support, while logic stays separate from presentation.

Enhanced Kickstart Template: New Domma projects now include built-in convention enforcement (CLAUDE.md, memory files) for AI-assisted development with Claude Code, Cursor, and similar tools.

Documentation: Comprehensive Template Files tutorial added to Router Showcase with 6 detailed sections covering all aspects of external template usage. Router now discoverable from the showcase hub.

releases.title: Motion Override & Effects Polish
releases.description:
Critical Fix: Resolved issue where reveal() and ripple() effects were disabled by CSS media queries even when JavaScript explicitly set respectMotionPreference: false.

Solution: Added data-force-animation attribute system to override CSS @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) queries. Showcase demo pages now display animations correctly regardless of system motion preferences.

Code Cleanup: Updated effects showcase pages to use consistent respectMotionPreference: false configuration, removing obsolete variable references across 3 showcase files.

releases.title: Typewriter Effect with Action Queue
releases.description:
Introduced Domma.effects.typewriter() with character-by-character text rendering, blinking cursor, and powerful action queue system.

Features:

  • Cursor styles: caret, block, underline
  • Action queue: render, wait, undoRender actions
  • Per-character entrance effects: fade, bounce, glow
  • Partial text deletion and configurable looping
  • Full control: pause/resume/restart

Performance: GPU acceleration and hardware-accelerated animations for buttery-smooth 60fps rendering. Perfect for hero banners, animated intros, and dynamic text displays.

All patron saint celebrations now feature realistic flutter animations and gentle vertical bobbing.
